children: Brazilian Critical Minerals
has continued to advance the development of its flagship Ema ionic clay rare earth project in the Apuí region of Amazonas state in northern Brazil.

The company’s management team recently travelled to Brazil, Canada, and the US as part of a broader effort to secure commercial relationships in the areas of permitting, offtake, financing, engineering, and magnesium sulphate supply.
The team is focused on locking in suitable customers and funding agreements, supported by a clear understanding of the proposed product, development requirements, and delivery schedule.

North America has emerged as one of the world’s most important rare earth jurisdictions due to its demand from strategic industries and downstream processing opportunities, fuelled by concerns over supply security.
Land Access Approval

Brazilian Critical Minerals has received approval from federal government agency INCRA Amazonas for a land access agreement covering mining activities on INCRA-controlled land, and has been issued with a separate certificate confirming there would be no impediments to environmental licensing.

Final exploration reports for both Ema tenements have been approved by Brazil’s National Mining Agency, while environmental licencing with the Amazonas Environmental Protection Institute and two trial mining licence applications remain pending.
These processes are being advanced alongside engineering and development planning that will allow the company to get on the ground at Ema and initiate construction activities.

Meanwhile, discussions continue with prospective offtake partners to evaluate Ema’s product specifications, development schedule, and potential supply arrangements, and detailed discussions on project funding are also progressing with several interested parties from Brazil and North America.
Magnesium Sulphate Plant

Several assessments have been completed on a magnesium sulphate plant owned by an established Brazilian producer, in which Brazilian Critical Minerals recently agreed to acquire a 90% strategic interest.

The deal will establish domestic Brazilian production of magnesium sulphate, which is the principal leaching reagent proposed for Ema’s in-situ recovery process and is expected to materially reduce the project’s exposure to Chinese reagent supply chains.
An initial process design has been drafted and a more detailed design will be carried out by the Brazilian engineering partner to allow for a capital cost estimate.
Brazilian Critical Minerals will then determine the plant’s nameplate capacity, complete the acquisition, and commence construction activities.
Initial production capacity is expected to supply approximately 50% of Ema’s magnesium sulphate requirements.
Key Roles Filled
Western Australian consultancy Altris Engineering has been chosen to lead Ema’s front-end engineering and design (FEED) program.

The search is underway for a Brazilian engineering partner to refine the processing plant and infrastructure design, confirm equipment selections, allow for firm vendor quotations, and update the capital estimate and schedule to Brazilian standards.

Brazilian Critical Minerals has appointed experienced process engineer Shahriar Masud to the role of project manager, overseeing construction activities for the Ema project and the magnesium sulphate plant.

Mr Masud has more than 20 years of experience in construction and commissioning, including leading the delivery of projects for Atlas Lithium and Sigma Lithium in Brazil and commissioning developments across Africa, Mongolia, and Kazakhstan.
His appointment is expected to strengthen the company’s technical and project delivery capabilities as it advances Ema and its integrated reagent supply strategy.

title: Brazilian Critical Minerals Advances Development of Flagship Ema Rare Earth Project
